finding.claim: The /admin/users/<uid>/ban endpoint runs do_ban(uid) for non-admin users. The admin check's failure is caught and only logged, so it never gates the action.
finding.source: Any caller who reaches the route with g.user set. The attacker controls uid (URL path) and the request. Admin rights are not required.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a protected state-changing operation (account ban).

trace.note: Route POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban is registered with no decorator, before_request, or role guard in this file.
For a non-admin, require_admin calls abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException, a subclass of Exception.
except Exception catches the 403 and only logs a warning. Execution continues. It also catches AttributeError if g.user is missing.
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally, so a non-admin bans any user.
Returns {ok: true}, so the attacker sees success.

finding.guards_checked: (1) require_admin at admin.py:9-11 raises for non-admins, but the exception is swallowed at line 18. (2) No return, re-raise, or early abort in the except block. (3) No route decorator or middleware in admin.py enforces admin. (4) unban at lines 24-28 has no try/except, so its 403 propagates and it is correctly gated; this is the intended pattern. (5) do_ban is a stub at lines 31-32, so real impact depends on its implementation, which was not visible. Auth middleware that sets g.user is not in this directory, so whether unauthenticated callers can reach the route is unverified. The admin bypass itself is confirmed by the code.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does abort(403), but its call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19), which only logs. No return, re-raise, or abort follows, and no decorator or middleware in admin.py gates the route at admin.py:14-15. The only other guard, unban at admin.py:26, has no try and is correctly gated, which shows the swallow in ban() is the defect.
verdict.reason: The 403 raised by require_admin at admin.py:11 is swallowed by the except at admin.py:18-19, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any caller whose g.user is a dict; trace lines all match the file. The attacker must be an authenticated user whose g.user is set (a missing or None g.user makes admin.py:19 raise AttributeError and return 500 before do_ban), and whether anonymous callers get g.user set depends on auth middleware that is not in this directory, so that part is unverified, but the authorization bypass for any authenticated low-privilege user is confirmed by admin.py:14-21.
